Hi Connor / Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the connector looks promising. Before we proceed to internal sign-off, Legal and Security have two blocking items around PII/PHI handling for the real-time clinical integration:

1) Retention windows: we need options for enforceable deletion windows (e.g., configurable 30/90/365 day TTLs) and an explanation of how deletion is implemented across hosted vs private deployments.
2) Redaction & reversible vs irreversible approaches: what do you support out of the box (field redaction, tokenization, pseudonymization), and what are the tradeoffs for downstream model quality?

I've attached a simple spreadsheet that lists our expected record types and suggested retention targets (see attachment: data_retention_table.xlsx). Legal wants a brief one-page response we can attach to our security review. Can you outline:

- recommended retention defaults for regulated PHI fields
- recommended redaction options by risk tier (e.g., direct identifiers vs contextual notes)
- where audit/evidence will be available (logs, deletion receipts, S3 object lifecycle info, etc.)

Thanks — Laura
Laura Chen
Director, Integrations

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Quick summary up front, then a proposed one-page response that you can attach to Legal:

Summary (TL;DR)
- Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) supports configurable retention TTLs at the route and customer level (30/90/365+ days). Deletion is implemented as a multi-step purge: metadata index deletion, KV cache eviction, and permanent object removal from backing storage (with lifecycle enforcement).
- Redaction options: field-level irreversible redaction (recommended for SSNs, MRNs), reversible tokenization (use sparingly, requires KMS-backed tokens), and selective pseudonymization for contextual notes to preserve model utility.
- Evidence: audit logs (immutable append-only), deletion receipts (signed event), and object lifecycle records available for Private customers. Hosted customers get time-limited audit exports and SLA-backed deletion workflows.

Attachment: brief playbook (attached: redaction_playbook_v1.pdf) — a short page you can forward to Legal.

Recommended defaults by risk tier (short bullets you can paste):
- Tier 1 (direct identifiers: SSN, MRN, DOB): default retention 30 days; irreversible redaction by default.
- Tier 2 (contact info, addresses): default retention 90 days; tokenization option if downstream requires deterministic linkage (token keys stored in customer-managed KMS for Private).
- Tier 3 (clinical notes, unstructured text): default retention 365 days; pseudonymization + selective field redaction recommended to preserve context for model performance.

Implementation notes (more detail for your engineers):
- Deletion is executed in three phases: 1) logical delete (removes from active index and routing), 2) KV-prefix purge (clears cached prefixes/kv cache entries), 3) physical purge job (removes objects from blob store based on TTL and retention policy) — each phase emits signed events into the audit stream.
- For hosted deployments we provide exportable deletion receipts and an SLA for deletion timelines; for Private customers the deletion jobs run in-customer infrastructure and customers control lifecycle policies and KMS.

Tradeoffs: irreversible redaction is safest for compliance but reduces downstream retrieval and context for few-shot prompts. Tokenization preserves linkability at the cost of additional KMS/rotation complexity. Pseudonymization is a middle path and often best for clinical NLP tasks.

Next steps: I can draft the one-page response for you and Legal by EOD today if that helps. Also — would a short screen-share showing where the deletion receipts and audit logs live be useful?

Cheers,
Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Laura — adding a few technical points to help Legal/Security evaluate risk and timelines:

- KV/Cache considerations: for real-time flows our runtime keeps a KV cache (prefix cache) to accelerate repeated prefixes. Cache entries are ephemeral and tied to session TTLs; we provide hooks to invalidate per-customer prefixes immediately when requested (API call: /admin/invalidate-prefix).
- Model & tokenization: if you choose reversible tokens we recommend storing token mapping in your KMS-backed vault. Redwood can optionally store encrypted token mappings in the customer's Private cluster if required by policy.
- Deletion evidence: the audit stream includes event IDs for logical delete, cache-invalidate, and blob purge. We can produce an exported bundle (signed JSONL) for the retention window showing timestamps and worker IDs.
- Orphaned artifacts: our physical purge job performs a consistency check and emits a report of orphaned blobs; Private customers can run verification weekly.

Suggested engineering implementation for MedSys:
- Phase 1 (pilot): start with Tier 1 irreversible redaction for identifiers + 90-day TTL for notes.
- Phase 2: add tokenization for contact records behind KMS for linking between systems.
- Phase 3: optimize model prompts and prompts templates to account for redacted tokens (we have guidance for prompt prefixes/operators).

Happy to put these bullets into Connor's one-pager.

—Karthik
Principal Applied ML Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Laura — quick confirmation from Security & Compliance:

- When customer-managed KMS is used in Private deployments, token mapping keys are encrypted with the customer KMS and Redwood operators do not have access to plaintext token mappings. We will include this statement in the one-pager and can provide an architectural diagram showing where keys live.
- Deletion receipt sample: we'll produce a signed JSONL that includes event_id, event_type (logical_delete / cache_invalidate / physical_purge), timestamp (RFC3339), resource_id, worker_id, and a signature header (HMAC-SHA256) — sample will be attached when I send the official evidence pack. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c_redwood_evidence_pack
- Next steps / timeline: Connor will draft the one-page response by EOD today; Security will assemble the sample deletion receipt and a short architecture diagram by Monday 2026-10-26. We can schedule a 30-minute screenshare next week to walk the Legal team through audit exports.
